name: Beauty-Tipps
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading, cut to Hall of Femme's
design. Everything that makes it a Snapchat pack is Hall of Femme's
and comes from the same two presets rather than being restated here:
the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite that turns speech into report, the stated 40px, the twenty
characters to a line, the freeform text box, the drag.
What makes it this show rather than that one is the face and the
colours: it is set in Syne Regular with picked words in Bebas Neue,
in a violet, a white and a red the user pairs between the type and
the card. Each is argued where it is stated.
The id is kebab-case ASCII because it is also the folder name and the
key everything else refers to; the name is the brand, hyphen and all.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: Where this show parts company with the pack it was cut from. Hall of
Femme sets its captions in Telegraf - a 200-weight hairline for the
block, the 800 for a picked word - on a hot pink card, in sixteen
pairings the user chooses between. This one is set in Syne Regular,
with picked words in Bebas Neue, in a deep violet, a white or a red
the user pairs per frame, on a card.
It used to set the caption on the photograph, in the violet alone,
held off the picture by a white halo. The show has since asked for
colours for the letters AND for a ground behind them, which is a
request for a card - the panel palette cannot exist without one (see
editor.paletteOf). So it is on the card its carded siblings use, and
what follows from that is written once, in content/README.md, under
'A channel that set its caption on the photograph may take the card
back'.
Capitals are inherited from the preset, and this pack could not
sensibly turn them off even if it wanted to. Bebas Neue has no lower
case - its lower-case codepoints are drawn as capitals - so a block
set in Syne's lower case would still have its picked words standing
in capitals, and the highlight would be carrying a difference nobody
chose. Set throughout, the capitals are the preset's own argument: at
40px with twenty characters to a line a caption is three short beats
rather than a paragraph, and beats are what capitals are for. It
costs nothing here either - both faces are display cuts, and their
capitals are what they were drawn for.

_comment_face: Syne Regular, the text weight of a display grotesque, and the
whole of what its family name costs is written out in
content/faces/syne-regular.json rather than repeated here. The
short version is that this app already carries Syne Bold, so the
cut has to be asked for by its full name or the block and a
neighbouring channel's highlight become the same request.
It is a text weight rather than a hairline, a far sturdier face
than re-belle's signature hand, and on a card of its own it needs
_comment_color: The show's violet, and the channel's own answer: what every frame
is set in until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no
colour of its own until it is given one (see state.textColorFor).
It opens the list in `colors` below, so the violet swatch is the
one shown as chosen on an untouched frame.
It is also the colour of a picked word - see `highlight` - which
makes it the colour of the whole caption, and whichever swatch the
user presses keeps it that way. What separates a picked
word here is the face and nothing else, which is Hall of Femme's
highlight exactly; the difference is that its two faces are two
cuts of one family and these two are two unrelated designs.

_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Bebas Neue, in the same violet as the
rest of the block. The colour is stated and it is the block's, so
the recolour draws exactly what its neighbours are drawn in and
the FACE is the whole of the difference - which is Hall of
Femme's highlight, with the one change that these two faces are
not two cuts of a family but two unrelated designs.
Which is why it never needed to become a box. Nothing here is
slightly different: Bebas Neue is a tall condensed face whose capitals
fill the em, so at the block's own 40px a picked word comes out
visibly taller and much narrower than the words either side of
it. It changes the shape of the line and not only its texture,
and it does it at a glance on a phone.
That two faces set at one size come out at two apparent sizes
costs nothing here, and it is worth saying why, because under a
boxed highlight or a fitted size it would cost something: there
is no rectangle to be sized to the taller letters, and no
per-line fit for the wider face to win, because the preset states
`fontSize` and that takes `uniformSize` out of the question (see
the note on two faces in content/README.md). The difference lands
on the letterforms and nowhere else.
Colour mode and word scope are the preset's, and the argument for
picking out words rather than lines lives there: a caption's line
breaks are wherever the sentence ran out of width, so picking a
LINE out picks out a fragment rather than a thought.
No shadow of its own any more. The white halo it used to restate
was there to match the block's on the photograph; with the card
back, the preset's null is right for both (see content/README.md).
_comment_panel: White, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
White because it is the first colour the show asked for and the
violet reads on it at once - the ground the old white halo was
trying to give each letter, given to the whole line instead. The
red is the other card a button away.
